title: Your profile: behavior, motivation, and emotion
text: Good morning, Al. Thank you for taking this assessment. Your debrief explores your behavior, how you do what you do; your drivers, why you do it; and your emotional intelligence, how you understand and regulate emotions and relate to others. Your Natural DISC style describes how you may behave when you feel comfortable. Your Adapted style describes how you adjust to your environment, including work. Your original debrief treats matching styles as reassuring: you are acting naturally, with no cause for concern about adaptation. When you change your behavior, you may experience some stress. Your chart uses red for Dominance, yellow for Influence, green for Steadiness, and blue for Compliance. Your scores run from zero to 100, with a reference line at 50. You can follow how strongly each preference appears in your profile.

title: Your DISC: Dominance and Influence
text: Your Dominance score is 93 in both your Natural and Adapted styles. You are strongly task-oriented, with urgency, determination, and a desire to tackle problems. You look for something to solve and want to see progress. You may feel frustrated when others move more slowly than you expect, or when a delegated task lacks the urgency you intended. You do not necessarily seek a fight, but you may be comfortable confronting an issue and going back and forth until your point is understood. You can notice when that determination helps and when your intensity prolongs the discussion. Your Influence score is 72 in your Natural style and 64 in your Adapted style. You may feel comfortable around people, explain difficult issues clearly, and bring creativity to people-related problems. Your Dominance supplies urgency and willpower; your Influence adds optimism and persuasion. You tend to look first at what you can do rather than what you cannot do. Your outlook may reassure others that things will work out. At work, your lower Adapted Influence suggests you become somewhat more circumspect and pragmatic.

title: Your DISC: pace, detail, and Persuading Conductor
text: Your Steadiness score moves from 22 in your Natural style to 8 in your Adapted style. You prefer a fast pace, variety, and several activities rather than a settled routine. You may become restless when things slow down, and your constant activity may leave you tired or overextended. You may not always have a poker face: others can see your frustration or excitement before you explain it. Your confidence may tell you that you can do it, and if it takes extra effort, you will work harder. You keep looking for improvements and problems to solve. Your original debrief puts that pace in perspective by saying 55% of people have a Steadiness score of 55 or higher. You are therefore working with many people who prefer more consistency and security than you do. You may be ready for a quick change while almost one in two people would resist it. Your Compliance dimension concerns rules, processes, details, accuracy, and analysis. In your debrief, you heard engineers and accountants described as typically high in Compliance because they want to get things right. Your lower Compliance makes you bolder and more willing to take chances before every detail is settled. Your combined style is a Persuading Conductor: you bring urgency, persuasive communication, confidence, and a drive to improve things. This as a profile shared by only 7% of the population, meaning the other 93% may not relate naturally to your approach. You can remember that your preferred pace and tolerance for risk may feel very different to someone else.

title: Your Driving Forces: knowledge, return, and surroundings
text: Your Driving Forces explore what makes an activity worth pursuing for you, across knowledge, utility, surroundings, others, power, and methodologies. Your Intellectual score is 17 and your Instinctive score is 58. Your Instinctive driver ranks fifth, and your Intellectual driver ranks eighth. You draw readily on gut judgment and past experience. You may not want to read another book or study a familiar subject at length when you already recognize a practical way forward. Your Resourceful driver is a leading priority: you want to maximize the return on your investment of time, money, and energy. You may lose interest when something feels wasteful, produces little useful feedback, or has no clear outcome. Your Selfless score is zero and ranks twelfth. You should not take that to mean you are selfish. You want your effort to be fruitful, with some kind of return. You may recognize the nickname Mr. ROI: when the return disappears, your interest may disappear too. For surroundings, your profile leans toward Objective. You want to understand how something functions and whether it works. Your Harmonious preference leaves room for how things look and feel, but your emphasis is on function. You may appreciate a good appearance while still asking whether the approach will produce results.

title: Your Driving Forces: helping, leading, and new approaches
text: For others, your profile leans toward Intentional. You are willing to help, but you want to see purpose, effort, and follow-through. You may lose interest when assistance continues without a response or useful outcome. You may recognize the fishing example: you can feed someone today, or teach them to fish. Your preference puts more emphasis on building capability and seeing progress than on continuing to do the work for someone indefinitely. Your Collaborative score is 8 and ranks eleventh. Your Commanding score is 81. You are comfortable directing work, taking charge, and having a voice in decisions. You may also want recognition for your contribution. You can connect that preference with your high Dominance while noticing how much room you leave for others. For methodologies, you lean toward Receptive rather than Structured. You are not drawn to an old method simply because it is familiar. You want innovation, a different approach, and a better way to get things done.

title: Your emotional intelligence and next conversation
text: Al, your emotional intelligence is the background programming behind your behavior. As your original debrief puts it, your emotions are the real bosses, influencing 90 to 95% of what you do. You can explore how you understand and manage yourself, and how you understand and relate to others. Your Self-Awareness score is 98. You are very aware of your emotions, impulses, and what you are feeling. You can use that awareness to notice what is happening before you respond. Your Self-Regulation score is 77. You often manage your emotions rather than letting your emotions manage you, but with your high Dominance you may still lose your cool. I'd suggest an ideal target around 90 to 95 for your Conductor profile, so you can notice where urgency turns into frustration. Your Motivation score is 81. You wake up ready to go without someone else needing to crank you up. You want success for yourself rather than relying entirely on external rewards. That's very good for you as a CEO. Your Social Awareness score is 76. You can connect with people's emotions while remaining pragmatic. You may distinguish people from tasks, but you can still ask whether you understand how someone feels when you are focused on a result. Your Social Regulation score is 84. You have a strong foundation for creating and maintaining your business and personal relationships. Your overall EQ as very good, and you should aim for scores in the 90s or above across every category because your Dominance is so high. You can bring your awareness, regulation, and understanding of others into your next conversation. Thank you, Al, for your attention, and I hope this has been helpful for you.
